parole.testo: From Coptic *ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲱϣ (*petrōš, “the flamingo”), from Egyptian dšr. Also found metathesized as Tunisian Arabic شَبْرُوش (šabrūš, “flamingo”).

parole.significato: Acacia spp. or Vachellia spp., especially Vachellia nilotica
parole.testo: Perhaps through Coptic ϣⲟⲛϯ (šonti), ultimately from Egyptian snḏt (/⁠ˈsantʼə/ < earlier /ˈsantʃʼat⁠/, “being feared, being respected, evoking reverence or respect; acacia”) stemming from its religious significance. Compare Akkadian 𒊭𒄠𒂅 (/⁠šamṭu, samṭu⁠/, “acacia”), a foreign loan suspected to be bo

parole.significato: an unknown kind of river fish, perhaps Petrocephalus bane
parole.testo: Apparently from Coptic ϣⲁⲗⲟⲩⲕⲓ (šalouki), ⲥⲁⲗⲟⲩⲕⲓ (salouki), from Egyptian šlq, alternative form of šrq, which also passed as شَرُّوك (šarrūk, “Schilbe”).
From the giant quarries of أُمّ الْصَوَّان (ʔumm al-ṣawwān) near أَسْوَان (ʔaswān), from Coptic ⲥⲟⲩⲁⲛ (souan), from Egyptian swnw s-wn:n-nw:W-T11:niwt
Borrowed from Coptic ⲕⲁϣⲱ (kašō), from Egyptian qš.
From Coptic (Sahidic Coptic ⲟⲉⲓⲡⲉ (oeipe), Bohairic Coptic ⲱⲓⲡⲉ (ōipe)), from Egyptian jpt.
